metadata.title: The next matching level for triangle-free graphs with bounded degree and an exact Bougard-Joret value
metadata.description:
Let T(d, m) be the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free graph with maximum degree at most d and matching number at most m, with no restriction on its order. We prove T(d, d + 1) = d² + d + 2 for every integer d ≥ 7. A shortest-odd-cycle deficit bound, followed by a five-type equality obstruction, first gives the same maximum on 2d + 3 vertices. The Tutte-Berge formula extends this bound to arbitrary order.

The attaining construction is due to Banak, Ekim and Taşkın; the contribution is the uniform upper bound. This settles the next-matching slice of the Ahanjideh-Ekim-Yıldız conjecture and, in particular, resolves the published bounds 184 ≤ T(13, 14) ≤ 185 in favor of 184.

As a consequence, the Bougard-Joret extremal function satisfies f(2d + 3, 2, d + 2) = d² + 4d + 2 for every d ≥ 7, an unbounded strict-interior discrepancy from the degree-sum prediction. The lower value is excluded by a structural theorem: every triangle-free graph on 2d + 3 vertices with maximum degree at most d and d² + d + 2 edges has two vertices with the same d neighbours, so its complement is not (d + 2)-connected. The full AEY conjecture remains open. Exact finite certificates and independent implementation checks support, but do not replace, the proofs.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/combinatorics/bougard-joret).
metadata.version_notes: New theorem: f(2d + 3, 2, d + 2) = d² + 4d + 2 for every d ≥ 7, closing the one-edge bracket of the previous text; every fixed-order maximizer has two vertices with a common d-neighbourhood. Title changed accordingly. The next-matching theorem T(d, d + 1) = d² + d + 2 is unchanged.
